rows.what the ink shows: The initial Greek letter has a compact closed oval around the upper part of a long downward stem. It has no separate open arms of psi.

Before the separate final que there are short faded strokes, a long connected horizontal run, a tall descending turn, and one clear dot. Even the enlarged contrast view does not expose enough individual letter counters to establish the full proposed three-word sequence.
Under the cancellation, the initial small curved s, a rounded dark o body, an isolated i dot above the deletion, and a terminal upright t survive. The middle horizontal is the deletion line.

The cancelled first word retains an initial curved c, compressed low bodies, a tall central d-like stroke and a dotted narrow stroke, ending with a separate full stop. After a gap the capital S-shaped stroke and i dot remain clear above the longer deletion.
The inserted glyph after quand has a descending left arm and a rising right arm ending in a small hook. It is uncrossed and lacks the tall looped/crossed stem of the nearby f glyphs.

rows.reading: comme dans les exemples, ou bornée
rows.what the ink shows: The line shows the low linked comme strokes, the taller d onset of dans, a distinct les group, then exemples with a long low middle and a descending loop near its end. A downward comma separates the two low ou humps from the tall initial b and connected ending of bornée.

The cancelled main glyph forms a pointed V-like body with its left stroke descending well below the cancellation and its right arm rising to it. The adjacent lower f has its own upright and crossbar. The main shape matches the uncancelled nu on the line immediately above, while the mu after that line's equals sign has a different upright-and-shoulder form.

A short opening parenthesis survives at the left of a curved numeral whose top curves upward and right and whose lower body meets the deletion line. The closing parenthesis continues below the line; the surviving numeral is a 6.

The opening is a rounded capital C followed by low connected letter groups and an i dot. Near the end a small separate oval is followed by low connected ns strokes; there is no independent final tall crossed t. The tall stroke passing through the last part descends from the f in the preceding line.
After log is a small oval-headed phi with a long descending stem, followed by a lower f and the parenthesized t. It lacks the capital Phi's broad loop and foot visible in equation (7) above.

The insertion above the crossed-out décroissante begins with a small open c, then a compressed on connection, a tall crossed t-like stroke followed by a separate i dot, and a low nue tail. The clearly written concave immediately above has a distinct closed a loop, which this inserted word lacks. This supports continue, subject to independent comparison.

After the opening parenthesis there is a separate oval a. The following word has a tall f with a descending return, the short crossbar of t, and two separate dots over the i positions; the final letters are compressed into a low horizontal connection.

Following the canceled log-formula, the putative word is an almost solid short horizontal black bar beneath the long cancellation stroke. No e counter, distinct s turn, or separate t ascender survives well enough to confirm est.

The sign between the left-hand expression and integral has two thick parallel horizontal bars, with a narrow white separation visible between their central portions. No diagonal inequality stroke is present.

Inside the right-hand parentheses the letter has an upright/slanting stem with a crossing rightward stroke, comparable to the t elsewhere in this same equation. It is not the small rounded double turn of an s.

The canceled opening has a tall initial l, an i dot and compressed middle strokes compatible with limite. The separate following à-like letter and its high accent/dot are visible. A dark angular remnant above the end of the first word may be an acute accent, but it intersects the deletion and does not securely distinguish limite from limité.

To the right of the opening phrase, a tall looped descending stem and raised horizontal dash followed by a short vertical stroke resemble f with superscript −1. Several long cancellation strokes obscure the joins. The original +infinity cannot be verified in its stated position; the spatial division between this mark and the following illegible span needs independent reconciliation.

The surviving right-hand material is crossed by several dark horizontal and diagonal strokes. There are low loops, a comma-like descending stroke and a terminal square-bracket-like shape, suggesting a mathematical expression rather than securely identifiable prose words; the internal symbols cannot be separated reliably.

Within the inverse-image parentheses there is a tall complement-shaped curved stroke, followed by an opening brace, a small closed oval zero, and a matching closing brace before the outer parenthesis.

The insertion above canceled positive has a recognizable initial c and a small following rounded loop. The middle letters are merged into a heavy nearly horizontal band with only tiny peaks; neither a separate crossed x nor a closed a counter remains distinguishable. The two candidate endings cannot be separated from this ink.
